title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standardized People Operations processes for hiring, employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and new managers as the single source of truth for common operational flows, timelines, and templates.

Key objectives:
- Reduce time-to-hire while preserving candidate experience and quality.
- Standardize onboarding to reduce new-hire time-to-productivity.
- Provide clear manager playbooks for performance management and continuous feedback.
- Ensure compliance with legal and security requirements during hire and onboarding.

Owners and scope:
- Primary owner: People Ops (owner_team: people-ops)
- Contributors: Hiring managers, Talent Acquisition, Security, IT, Finance (for offers), Legal when required
- Applies to: all full-time employees, contractors, and long-term interns unless otherwise noted

Section 1 - Hiring process (requisition -> offer)

1.1 High-level flow:
1) Hiring manager creates requisition in Greenhouse (job code + role profile + hiring band).
2) People Ops reviews and approves requisition (SLA: 2 business days).
3) Talent Acquisition sources and screens candidates.
4) Interview loop executed (panel interviews + role-specific exercises).
5) Debrief and scorecard consolidation.
6) Compensation and offer approval via People Ops + Finance.
7) Offer extended, candidate acceptance, background check initiated (if applicable), start date confirmed.

1.2 Requisition checklist for managers (must complete before People Ops approval):
- Role brief: one-paragraph summary, responsibilities, must-have skills, nice-to-have skills
- Salary band and suggested level (reference compensation band matrix)
- Interview team and proposed loop (list of interviewers and roles)
- Diversity sourcing plan (recommended: 2 diverse-slate requirement for senior roles)
- Estimated target start date

1.3 Interviewing best practices:
- Use the standard scorecard in Greenhouse for every candidate. Scorecards must include: role fit, technical capability, communication, ownership, and culture fit.
- Behavioral questions should be consistent across candidates for the same role.
- Assign at least one interviewer focused on mentoring/behavioral fit and one on technical depth.
- Interviewers must avoid salary/compensation negotiation (redirect to People Ops).
- Debrief within 48 hours after final interview.

1.4 Offer and approvals:
- Offers require manager, People Ops, and Finance approval for total compensation above band midpoint.
- Standard offer SLA: People Ops to produce offer package within 5 business days after final approval.
- For executive or highly strategic hires, notify Legal and the Head of People Ops early in the process.

Section 2 - New hire onboarding (Day 0 -> 90)

2.1 Onboarding philosophy:
Redwood's onboarding emphasizes clarity, early wins, and cross-functional introduction. The aim is to get new hires to a meaningful contribution within 30-60 days and full productivity within 90 days.

2.2 Pre-start (Day 0) checklist - People Ops / IT / Manager:
- People Ops: send Welcome packet (offer letter, benefits overview, first-week schedule, contact list) at least 7 calendar days before start.
- IT: create account requests (Okta, Google Workspace, Slack) and order hardware (laptop + peripherals) no later than 3 business days before start; confirm delivery.
- Security: initiate any necessary background checks and NDA paperwork.
- Manager: send first-week agenda, 30-60-90 draft goals template, and team announcement.

2.3 First day (Day 1) agenda - Manager to lead:
- Morning: team welcome, HR orientation (benefits, payroll, policies), security training enrollment.
- Lunch: team intro (virtual or in-person depending on location).
- Afternoon: role-specific setup (access to code repos, tickets, internal docs) and first small task assigned.

2.4 First week objectives:
- Complete mandatory trainings: Security Basics, Code of Conduct, Data Handling.
- Access: confirm necessary service accounts and repo access.
- Shadowing sessions with direct collaborator(s).
- Initial 30-60-90 goals reviewed and adjusted with manager.

2.5 30-60-90 day plan (template):
- 30 days: orientation complete, primary systems access, first deliverable shipped, one feedback checkpoint.
- 60 days: increased ownership of 1-2 components, mid-point feedback conversation, identify growth areas.
- 90 days: full ownership of role responsibilities, performance checkpoint, calibration for compensation or role adjustments if needed.

2.6 New-hire manager responsibilities (checklist):
- Schedule recurring 1:1s starting week 1 (weekly for first 12 weeks recommended).
- Provide clear success criteria for first 90 days and connect new hire with mentors.
- Run the 30-day and 90-day feedback conversations using standardized templates and document outcomes in the HRIS.

Section 3 - Performance and feedback cycles

3.1 Cadence and types of reviews:
- Ongoing continuous feedback: documented in weekly 1:1s and manager notes.
- Quarterly check-ins: lightweight calibration between manager and employee (optional for ICs, required for managers).
- Formal performance cycle: annual review (calendar: November review cycle with reviews finalized by December 15) and mid-year calibration in June.

3.2 Manager responsibilities during performance cycles:
- Maintain regular feedback and written notes in the HRIS.
- Write measurable objectives and outcomes for the annual review period.
- Complete calibration matrix and submit ratings by the deadline.
- Provide actionable development plans for any below-expectation ratings.

3.3 Calibration and rating guidelines (summary):
- Rating buckets: Exceeds Expectations, Meets Expectations, Needs Improvement.
- Calibration: managers must provide objective evidence (projects, metrics, peer feedback) to support ratings.
- Appeals: employees can request a calibration review within 10 business days of receiving rating. People Ops facilitates the appeal.

3.4 Continuous feedback norms:
- Encourage timely feedback (within 2 business days of event) and celebrate wins publicly.
- Use 1:1s for developmental coaching; use EOY review for summative evaluation.
- Managers should document coaching conversations and agreed-upon actions in the HRIS.

3.5 Performance improvement and remediation:
- For pattern of performance concerns, manager should: 1) Document concerns and prior coaching, 2) Build a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with measurable goals and a 30-90 day timeline, 3) Engage People Ops to review and sign off, 4) Reassess at the end of the PIP and determine next steps.

Section 4 - Manager playbook: practical templates and timelines

4.1 Creating a requisition (quick steps):
1) Open Greenhouse -> New Requisition -> select job family and level
2) Paste role brief and attach scorecard
3) Propose interview panel and expected timeline
4) Save and notify People Ops for approval

4.2 Interview debrief template (to use in Greenhouse):
- Candidate: [name]
- Panel: [names]
- Role fit (1-5): [score] - notes
- Technical (1-5): [score] - notes
- Communication & collaboration (1-5): [score] - notes
- Decision: [hire / nope / hold] - rationale

4.3 Offer checklist for managers before extending an offer:
- Confirm final compensation and equity proposal with People Ops and Finance
- Confirm signatory and reporting line
- Plan first-day schedule and immediate onboarding tasks
- Prepare team announcement and buddy assignment

4.4 Running feedback conversations (scripted prompts):
- Opening: "I want to share what I've observed and give you space to share your perspective."
- Specifics: cite 2-3 concrete examples of behaviors or deliverables
- Impact: explain how the behavior affects the team or product
- Development: propose 1-2 concrete actions and check-ins
- Close: agree on timelines and next check-in date

Section 5 - Compliance, security and records

5.1 Mandatory checks and training:
- Background checks: role-dependent; mandatory for customer-facing and finance roles.
- Security training: must be completed in first 10 business days.
- Access reviews: manager must confirm access lists on day 30 and day 90.

5.2 Recordkeeping and retention:
- Offer letters, signed NDAs, and background-check results are stored in the HRIS and Legal Vault.
- Performance records (reviews, PIPs) retained per policy for a minimum of 3 years.

Section 6 - Templates and resources (links)
- Role brief template: /confluence/templates/role-brief
- 30-60-90 template: /confluence/templates/30-60-90-plan
- Greenhouse scorecard: /greenhouse/scorecards/default
- Offer letter templates: /confluence/templates/offer-letters
- HRIS manual: /confluence/people-ops/hris-manual
- IT & Security onboarding checklist: /confluence/company-handbook/new-hire-it-and-security-setup-2025

Appendix A - Example 30/60/90 (engineering IC)
- 0-30: Set up dev environment; fix a minor bug; attend architecture overview; complete security training.
- 31-60: Deliver a small feature; pair with code owner on an internal tool; identify areas to optimize for latency or cost.
- 61-90: Own a feature from design to deploy; present a 90-day retrospective and 6-month plan.

Appendix B - Escalation contacts
- People Ops general: people-ops@redwood-inference.example.com
- IT helpdesk: it-support@redwood-inference.example.com
- Security: security@redwood-inference.example.com
